review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions and lemmas it uses: laplaceBeltrami_zero and complexLaplaceBeltrami_ofReal in ChartDerivativeNeZeroTransfer.lean, the laplaceBeltrami_add/_sub/_const call sites, and BundleRankOne. The file declares no @[simp] lemmas and no simp sets. The `simp only [...]` calls are explicit, so there are no competing rules or loops to report. The one issue is the missing canonical simp rule for constant functions under laplaceBeltrami. It is a moderate-confidence finding: I did not check every downstream simp call, and I could not run Lean to see whether `simp` already closes such goals through other routes. The `Complex.ofRealCLM` unfolding in `laplaceBeltrami_add`, `laplaceBeltrami_sub` and `hsub` is repeated, but that is proof duplication rather than a simp-interface defect, so I left it out.

findings.excerpt:
lemma laplaceBeltrami_const (g : SmoothMetric E M) (c : ℝ) (x : M) :
    laplaceBeltrami g (fun _ => c) x = 0 := by
  simp [laplaceBeltrami, Function.comp_def]
findings.problem: This is the canonical normalisation `laplaceBeltrami g (fun _ => c) x = 0`. It is unconditional, its right-hand side is strictly smaller, and it cannot cycle. It has no `@[simp]` attribute, so it is consumed only through explicit `rw [..., laplaceBeltrami_const]` (lines 64 and 121). The same fact already exists as `laplaceBeltrami_zero` for `c = 0`, proved by the identical `simp [laplaceBeltrami, Function.comp_def]` call. Neither lemma is simp, so every site where a constant function reaches `laplaceBeltrami` needs a manual rewrite or an unfolding `simp [laplaceBeltrami, ...]`. `complexLaplaceBeltrami_ofReal` is one such site; it applies `laplaceBeltrami_zero` by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `laplaceBeltrami_const` as `@[simp]`. Its LHS is a lambda-with-constant-body pattern, so it should match as a head-`laplaceBeltrami` rewrite. Then either drop `laplaceBeltrami_zero` and use `laplaceBeltrami_const g 0 x` at its single use in `complexLaplaceBeltrami_ofReal`, or restate `laplaceBeltrami_zero` as a `simpa using laplaceBeltrami_const g 0 x` corollary so there is one canonical rule. After that, the `rw [..., laplaceBeltrami_const]` steps in `weightedLaplacian_shift` and `laplaceBeltrami_small_jets_on_compact` can be left to `simp`, and the unfolding `simp [laplaceBeltrami, Function.comp_def]` calls become `simp`.
findings.benefit: Constant-function Laplacians normalise to 0 without unfolding the definition of `laplaceBeltrami`. The near-duplicate lemmas collapse into one simp rule, so callers do not have to choose between `_zero` and `_const`.
